title: Private clusters: identity propagation drift causing role-mapping inconsistencies and missing audit events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customers running Private (VPC/on-prem) clusters with KMS envelope rotation enabled are observing two correlated failures after last control-plane rollout: 1) IdP assertions with long group/role claims are intermittently losing the tenant role claim during the assertion-to-principal transformation, causing RBAC policies to not be applied; 2) audit events for the same sessions are occasionally written without the KMS envelope id or are omitted entirely. Impacted customers reported access denials and missing audit trails which violates their compliance requirements. Root cause appears to be a race between the assertion normalization path (string chunking/truncation edge case) and the KMS envelope refresh codepath that writes audit payload metadata. This ticket tracks the urgent patch, rollout, verification, and customer updates.
impact_summary: Affects 3 enterprise Private deployments (multi-tenant private control plane). Symptoms: unexpected 403s for previously allowed API routes, absence of corresponding audit lines in the compliance S3 bucket, and SSO re-login required to rehydrate roles. Customers include two high-compliance financial customers and one healthcare partner; regulatory risk if not fixed within 72 hours.
reproducible_steps: Deploy a Private cluster with KMS envelope rotation enabled and IdP returning >12KB group claim payload
Perform an SSO login that includes >150 group entries (simulated IdP assertion)
Observe control-plane logs for assertion-transformation warnings (look for 'claim_truncate' or 'assertion_chunked')
Inspect user RBAC mapping in the cluster: role claim absent or mapped to default role
Check audit sink: search for audit events from the same session; look for 'audit_write_failed' or entries with missing 'envelope_id' in metadata
temporary_mitigations: Advise customers to disable KMS envelope rotation (workaround) until patch is applied
Suggest limiting group claim size via IdP filter for affected tenants
Roll back last control-plane change on the smallest impacted cluster if customer requests immediate revert
fix_summary: Short-term patch: make assertion transformer tolerant to large claim blocks by switching from naive chunk-and-truncate to stream-aware parsing; add a defensive reconciliation step that preserves role claims when chunking is detected. Also harden KMS audit writer to attach a provisional envelope id prior to rotation and retry persisted writes on envelope mismatch. Changes are isolated to the private control-plane code paths and include feature-flag gating for canary rollout.
verification_steps: Deploy canary to a single private control plane with feature-flag enabled
Simulate IdP assertions with >12KB claims and verify principal mapping includes tenant role
Run end-to-end flows for affected customers and confirm 200 responses for previously failing API calls
Validate audit events are written with non-empty 'envelope_id' and appear in compliance S3 within 60s
Monitor canary for 24h for regression signals: error rate, increased latency, audit write failures
postmortem: pending - will link final RCA and remediation timeline once hotfix is validated and rolled out
